question: Name the transuranium element with atomic number 106, created by bombarding californium⁻²⁴⁹ with oxygen⁻¹⁸ nuclei.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Seaborgium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seaborgium,** with the **atomic number 106,** is classified as a transuranium element. It is artificially created by** bombarding californium⁻²⁴⁹ with oxygen⁻¹⁸ nuclei**.
 
• As a synthetic element, seaborgium is solid at room temperature and belongs to the transition metal group. Its most stable isotope, seaborgium⁻²⁶⁶, has a half-life of 27.3 seconds.
 
• In 1994, the proposal to name element 106 "seaborgium" was made in tribute to Glenn T. Seaborg, the scientist credited with discovering the transuranium elements.
 
• Seaborg, an American chemist, was awarded the 1951 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his pioneering work in the field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dubnium (Db)** is an artificially generated radioactive transuranium element situated in Group Vb of the periodic table, with an atomic number of 105. The discovery of dubnium, much like that of rutherfordium (element 104), has been the subject of contention between Soviet and American scientists.
 
• **Hassium (Hs)** is another artificially produced element belonging to the transuranium group, with an atomic number of 108. It was first synthesized and identified in 1984 by researchers from West Germany at the Institute for Heavy Ion Research (Gesellschaft für Schwerionenforschung [GSI]) in Darmstadt.
 
• **Copernicium** is a synthetic chemical element characterized by the symbol Cn and atomic number 112. Its known isotopes are profoundly radioactive and have exclusively been generated within laboratory settings.
